The Γ★ showcase — discrete + continuous, capped + uncapped

One DGP, every experiment: the sensitivity parameter Γ★ = 5 is readable off the propensity by algebra (logistic-in-S, never clipped), so every method runs at the single flagged matched Γ with nothing tuned. 5 seeds; every raw per-seed policy persisted; the 15-job wave ran simultaneously on the CARC cluster Gurobi license in ~75 minutes.

1. The data-generating process

Aggressive therapy under hidden vitality with a fixed burden; the design follows the synthetic conventions of the MSM literature (logistic-in-hidden-confounder propensity and a level-shift confounder as in Kallus-Mao-Zhou 2019 and Hess/Frauen et al. ICLR 2026; uniform observed covariate; burden per the budgeted policy-learning tradition). N = 600 (discrete) / 400 train + 4000 test (continuous) per seed; 5 seeds; every raw per-seed policy persisted.

X~Unif{−1,…,1} (7 levels; continuous: X~Unif[−1,1]),S∣X∈{±1}, P(S=+1∣X)=σ(10X)
e(X,S)=σ(−1.5X+12ln(5)S)
μ0=8S,μ1=9S+3X−1,Y(t)=μt+𝒩(0,0.62)
CATE(X)=(2σ(10X)−1)+3X−1,CATE(0)=−1
Γ★ by inspection (the design's central property). The propensity is logistic in the hidden S with coefficient ½ln(5) and range [0.091, 0.909] — no clipping ever occurs — so the selection odds ratio between the S-arms is exactly Γ★ = 5 at every X, by algebra (verified numerically to 1e-12, and empirically: fitted per-level odds ratios 4.5–5.5 at n = 20,000). Every method runs at the single flagged matched Γ = 5 with nothing tuned; the Γ-grid appears only to show misspecification behavior. The fitted marginal propensity lies between the two S-extremals, so the Γ★ odds-box around it covers every unit's true weight: a correctly specified sensitivity model with a KNOWN parameter.

The single number that decides whether a transport / balance term can help at all. Range 1.00 here. Flat at 0.5 means the covariate carries NO information about the confounder, and no X-balancing device can constrain it; a steep curve means the confounder is x-trackable.

The vertical gap between the green and purple curves IS the confounding: two units at the same x get treated at different rates purely because of the hidden state. Range [0.091, 0.909], no clipping, so overlap holds everywhere and the odds ratio between the two states is exactly Gamma* at every x.

Where this is positive the oracle treats: 43% of the covariate range. This is the signal every method is trying to recover; everything else on this page is about what stands between the data and this curve.

Solid = S=+1, dashed = S=-1; red = treated, blue = control. The hidden state moves outcomes by 18.0 on average while the treatment moves them by 1.5 — the confounder is the larger effect, which is exactly what makes the benchmark hard.

Averaged over the hidden state S, so this is what the treatment is actually worth at each x. The two curves cross at x = 0.14 — that crossing IS the oracle's decision boundary, and every method is trying to find it from confounded data.

Dashed = the arm means visible in infinite CONFOUNDED data; solid = the true potential-outcome means. Mean absolute bias 0.68 in the treated arm and 0.61 in the control arm. Both arms are biased in the SAME direction here, which is why the contrast can look far milder than either arm on its own.

Black = the truth, blue = what infinite CONFOUNDED data would show. The vertical gap is pure bias. It matters only where it crosses zero: the two disagree about whether to treat on 18% of the covariate range, and that disagreement is the entire opportunity for a sensitivity-model method.

Reference values (exact): never-treat 0, all-treat -1; discrete oracle 0.847 uncapped / 0.727 capped(30%); continuous oracle 0.732 (realized, 5x4000 draws) / capped-oracle 0.628 (treats x > 0.40). The 30% cap < 43% oracle mass: genuinely scarce.

Continuous verdict. Two corrections since the first version of this report, both against us and both kept. First, the sharp column was originally measured with EQUALLY SPACED bin edges and analytic bin-mean evaluation while every other method was scored on test draws; re-measured properly that plug-in bound came to 0.567, ahead of IPW-O-W's 0.549, where this report had shown it losing. Second, the plug-in was the wrong baseline entirely and has been REPLACED by Hess et al.'s efficient estimator (see the card above).

Where that leaves the continuous arm. The transport term's contribution is unchanged, because it is measured against O-X under identical conditions: uncapped O-W 0.549 vs box-only 0.383 (+0.17). Against the corrected sharp baseline O-W leads in both regimes here.

L behaves as everywhere else: L = ∞ is Γ-inert and poor, L ≈ 2–3 is the sweet spot, L ≤ 1 over-smooths.

Which coupling should be the headline? α = 10 vs α = 4

The question. The coupling ablation peaks at α = 4, so the whole continuous arm was re-run there (same n = 400, same 5 seeds, same Γ grid, same everything else). The two settings disagree about which is "better", and they disagree for a reason worth understanding rather than resolving by picking the bigger number.

α = 10 looks better against an ABSOLUTE ceiling: O-W recovers 74% of what the oracle could add over never-treat, vs 38% at α = 4. α = 4 looks better against an unconfoundedness-assuming baseline, and its margin over box-only O-X is larger. Part of that is that the unconfounded baselines COLLAPSE at α = 4 — not purely because we do better.

α = 4 is also the more moderate DGP: corr(x, S) = 0.704 vs 0.837.

A decision maker who is actually rational

The Γ★ DGP above has a problem worth stating plainly. Its CATE μ1−μ0 = S + 3x − 1 rises in x, while its propensity σ(−1.5x + ½ln5·S) falls in x. The units who benefit most were historically treated least, which reads as an incompetent decision maker rather than a confounded one.

The fix keeps the confounding and removes the incompetence: the decision maker observes a private prognostic signal S that the analyst does not, and acts rationally on both arguments.

x~U(−1,1),S=±1 w.p. 12,S⟂x
e(x,S)=Pr(T=1∣x,S)=σ(2x+12ln(5)S)
Y0=2S+ε,Y1=Y0+2x+S+ε′⟹CATE=2x+S

Treatment probability rises in x and in S; the benefit rises in x and in S. Both moves are correct, so the hidden signal is now a reason the decision maker was right. The x-measurable oracle treats x > 0. Because e is never clipped the S-odds ratio is exactly 5 at every x (verified to 1.6e−14), so the matched Γ★ is exact just as above; overlap stays in [0.14, 0.86] and the headroom is 0.489.

O-W wins 8 of 11 configurations, not all of them. A properly optimised Hess with k-NN nuisances is a genuine competitor and takes three of them, all in the δ=2 / β0=5 corner. The recommended configuration is the widest win rather than a lucky one, and O-W is also about seven times more stable there (±0.074 against ±0.544). A 54-configuration smoke sweep passed 39, so this is a broad region rather than a knife edge.

On the Hess instantiation. "Hess (paper)" is the authors' repository pipeline verbatim ({64,32} ReLU networks for every nuisance and the policy — their code differs from their Table 5 — Adam lr 10−3, batch 64, ≤300 epochs, patience 10, disjoint 50/50 split). The k-NN row is a nuisance-sensitivity diagnostic, not a rival method. The aligned baseline carries large seed-to-seed variance at n = 400 and is data-hungry: on KMZ it scores 0.21 at n = 400 against 1.19 at the paper's own n = 5000.
